title: On the Information Required for Feedback Control
authors: Matthew P. Leighton, Jose M. Betancourt, Thierry Emonet, Benjamin B. Machta, Michael C. Abbott
abstract: Biological systems across scales, along with many engineering problems, must control noisy systems with limited information. Here we study information-limited feedback control of stochastic systems to achieve target steady states, and derive a lower bound on the information rate from controlled system to controller. This framework allows us to obtain performance-information Pareto frontiers for wide-ranging control problems with limited information. For systems with state-independent passive dynamics, the bound is saturated by an explicit optimal control protocol which probabilistically time-reverses the passive dynamics. We showcase these results through applications to nonlinear particle localization, microbial navigation, and experimentally realized information engines.
summary: This paper develops a general framework to quantify the minimum amount of information needed to control a stochastic physical system toward a target steady state. It derives a fundamental lower bound relating this required information rate to the passive entropy production rate of the uncontrolled dynamics. This has implications for understanding optimal feedback control in fields ranging from biology to engineering.
main_problem: The study focuses on deriving fundamental lower bounds for the information rate required by a controller to guide a stochastic system toward a desired steady state.
main_result: A key theoretical result establishes that the minimum required information rate is bounded below by the passive entropy rate of the uncontrolled dynamics ($\dot{S}_p \le \dot{T}_{x 	o 	ext{d}x_c}$).
method: The analysis employs information theory, relating changes in system entropy to mutual and conditional entropies derived from stochastic differential equations (SDEs).
model_or_system: The models involve general stochastic systems with passive dynamics (e.g., Brownian motion, bit flipping) coupled to an active control input. The framework is general but applied to localization and navigation problems.
key_observables: Information Rate ($\dot{T}_{x 	o 	ext{d}x_c}$), Passive Entropy Rate ($\dot{S}_p$), Performance functional ($P[ho]$).
important_parameters: The analysis is sensitive to the nature of passive dynamics (e.g., state-independent vs. general) and operates in limits like low information content ($\epsilon \ll 1$).
main_assumptions: Assumptions include stationarity for steady-state analysis, and approximations using instantaneous rates or Gaussian distributions when deriving explicit protocols.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the relationship between performance, entropy, and required information rate for various control scenarios (e.g., Brownian particle localization).
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the stochastic system dynamics to establishing the core information-theoretic bound ($\dot{S}_p \le \dot{T}_{x 	o 	ext{d}x_c}$), deriving optimal time-reversal protocols for specific cases, and applying this framework to diverse physical examples like particle localization and information engines.
why_interesting: The work provides a rigorous information-theoretic lens—a generalized second law—for understanding control in complex, noisy systems, which has parallels in open quantum system dynamics where dissipation is key.
